## Why a separate entry point

`catcheR_10Xcatch()` slices read 1 at fixed offsets: `cut -c 1-16` for the cell
ID and `cut -c 17-28` for the UMI. PIPseq breaks that assumption. Read 1 carries
0–3 phasing bases followed by a four-tier barcode separated by constant linkers:

```
[0-3 nt phasing] bc1(8) ATG bc2(6) GAG bc3(6) TCGAG bc4(8) [index 3] ACG (dT)n
```

The fields therefore move from read to read and must be matched, not sliced.
Read 2 is unchanged from the 10X design: the construct is read from the
enrichment primer, so `revcomp(reference)` sits at positions 1–23, followed by
`revcomp(UCI)` and `revcomp(barcode)`.

Two further consequences:

* **There is no usable UMI.** The 3 nt molecular index has only 64 values and
  collides constantly, so every metric counts **reads**. The column keeps the
  name `UMIxUCI` for continuity with `catcheR_filtercatch()`.
* **Matching the linkers is not enough.** Requiring only `ATG`/`GAG`/`TCGAG`
  admits roughly fifteen times more reads than requiring the whole oligo, almost
  all of them chance matches in construct or adapter sequence. `.pip_parse_r1()`
  also requires the index, the constant `ACG` and the oligo-dT.

## Extraction

```{r}
library(catcheR)

res <- catcheR_pipcatch(
  folder         = "data",
  fastq.read1    = "AB019b_BC_S4_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz",
  fastq.read2    = "AB019b_BC_S4_L001_R2_001.fastq.gz",
  barcodes.genes = c("rc_barcodes_genes_set1.csv", "rc_barcodes_genes_set2.csv"),
  set.names      = c("set1", "set2"),
  set.sizes      = c(100L, 60L),
  output_dir     = "Output/pipcatch",
  sample_name    = "AB019b"
)
res
```

Pooled experiments are often supplied as several barcode CSVs written in
opposite orientations. `catcheR_pipcatch()` resolves each file against the
barcodes actually observed in the reads and reports what it did, rather than
trusting the file:

```
set1: 100 barcodes, as given (fwd 52 / rc 0)
set2: 60 barcodes, reverse-complemented (fwd 0 / rc 40)
```

## Thresholds

Both of catcheR's automatic estimators assume more depth than a PIPseq
enrichment library usually has, so `catcheR_pipcatch()` reports what they
*would* choose instead of silently applying one.

`mode = "noise"` is undefined once more than `1 / 1.35 = 74.07 %` of
(cell, UCI) pairs are singletons: the term `1 - perc_1/100 * 1.35` goes
negative and the original subsets with a negative index. `mode = "bimodal"`
needs a genuine valley in the `UMIxUCI` histogram; at low depth the only local
minimum is a gap in the tail, and taking it discards almost every cell.

```{r}
flt <- catcheR_pip_filtercatch(res, UMI.count = 0, percentage = 15, ratio = 2)
flt$filter_returns
```

The threshold is a **read count per (cell, UCI) pair**, compared with a strict
`>`. `UMI.count = 1` therefore means "at least 2 reads" and discards every
single-read UCI. Note also that `ratio` is inert at `UMI.count = 0`: every
surviving cell sits at `UMIpercentagexUCI == 100` and takes the escape clause in
the `ValidCell` rule. It only matters once the threshold is raised.

## Empty cells

`catcheR_pip_nocatch()` selects reads carrying the no-insertion reference. That
sequence is an argument rather than a string inside a shell script, because the
junction is construct-specific: when the cassette is absent the vector flanks
fuse and regenerate `TACGCGTTCATCTGGGGGAGCCG`, which also places the downstream
constant 21 nt earlier in read 2 than in a cassette-bearing read.

```{r}
noc <- catcheR_pip_nocatch(res, filtered = flt, threshold = 0)
```

## Joining to the expression matrix

PIPseeker writes `barcodes.tsv.gz` as the same 28 nt concatenated four-tier
barcode that `catcheR_pipcatch()` extracts, so the join is a direct match and no
whitelist translation is needed. Confirm once per chemistry with
`nchar(readLines(gzfile(cells)))[1]`.

```{r}
obj <- catcheR_pip_seurat(
  res, filtered = flt, empty = noc,
  mtx      = "AB019b_gex.scRNA.filtered.matrix.mtx.gz",
  features = "AB019b_gex.scRNA.filtered.features.tsv.gz",
  cells    = "AB019b_gex.scRNA.filtered.barcodes.tsv.gz",
  protein.coding = protein_coding_genes,
  sample_id = "AB019b", rename = TRUE, subset.valid = TRUE
)
```

Every cell gains `shRNA`, `gene`, `set`, `UCI`, `barcode`, `UMIxUCI`,
`reads_total`, `n_UCI`, `ValidCell`, `is_empty` and `catcheR_status`. With
`rename = TRUE` the cells are renamed to catcheR's
`cellID_UMIxUCI_barcode_gene_UCI`.

When you merge several samples, attach the metadata **before** the merge:
`Seurat::merge(add.cell.ids = ...)` prefixes the barcodes, after which the 28 nt
key no longer matches.

## Report

```{r}
catcheR_pip_report(
  folder = "data",
  fastq.read1 = "AB019b_BC_S4_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz",
  fastq.read2 = "AB019b_BC_S4_L001_R2_001.fastq.gz",
  ref_csv = c("rc_barcodes_genes_set1.csv", "rc_barcodes_genes_set2.csv"),
  set_names = c("set1", "set2"), set_sizes = c(100L, 60L),
  outdir = "pipcatch_out"
)
```

This re-runs the extraction and knits the step-by-step document bundled at
`system.file("rmd", "catcheR_pipcatch_report.Rmd", package = "catcheR")`.
